A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DHAT research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original adversarial-robustness experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Imagenette, including ablations, transfer attacks, attention analyses, and learning curves.

after.justification: V2 retains original CIFAR experiments and reports additional ImageNet-1K, synthetic-data, attention-extractor, computational-cost, and inverse-attack-strength results.

M1.justification: Equation (10) changes FLOE from a positive orthogonal-residual norm to its negative, reversing the stated optimization direction of a central regularizer; Algorithm 1 confirms the negative sign. V2 also permits alternative attention extractors. The PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: V2 adds full ImageNet-1K classification beyond the earlier CIFAR and Imagenette coverage. The Imagenette benchmark panel disappears from Table 1, but Imagenette remains in the threshold and attention analyses, so the dataset is not entirely removed.

E2.justification: The principal defense comparators remain MART, AWP, FSR, CFA, UIAT, and SGLR. New Table 8 adds comparisons with Integrated Gradients, SOLO, and SAM as alternatives to Grad-CAM within DHAT; these are component comparisons rather than new defense baselines.

E3.justification: V2 introduces an ImageNet protocol using 50 epochs, two-step PGD, epsilon 4/255, and step size 1/255, while retaining the CIFAR protocol. Added experiments use 50K generated samples per CIFAR dataset, varied inverse-attack strengths, and timing with batch size 128. The separate 200-epoch learning-curve experiment is removed.

E4.justification: V2 adds computational-efficiency analysis, inverse-attack-strength versus overfitting tests, synthetic-data analysis, and attention-extractor comparisons. It removes v1's t-SNE feature-separation analysis and learning-curve analysis. Existing DHLR/FLOE ablations, parameter sensitivity, transfer attacks, and attack-magnitude analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. V2's description of an IoU analysis as statistical does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds ImageNet-1K results and Tables 3, 5, 7, and 8, while removing the Imagenette benchmark panel and two appendix analyses. Matched CIFAR, architecture, component-ablation, and transfer-table values remain unchanged. For example, CIFAR-10 DHAT AA remains 53.10%; ImageNet-1K AA of 41.70% is a new result under different conditions.

T1.justification: The FLOE definition in Equation (10) receives a substantive sign correction. Other equations retain their mathematical content apart from notation changes such as the background subscript S becoming B. No new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The three central contributions—identifying background bias, introducing DHAT, and improving robustness and generalization—remain. V2's abstract explicitly extends the state-of-the-art claim to ImageNet-1K, while retaining the original method and integration claims.

C2.justification: V2 strengthens causal interpretations, explicitly treating Robust Gap as quantifying spurious-correlation strength, and expands the explanation of FLOE. It adds interpretations of synthetic-data results and limitations involving segmentation quality versus computational cost, while removing the earlier feature-distribution and learning-curve interpretations.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code link, complete pseudocode, CAM-based foreground/background construction details, and settings for ImageNet, generated-data, and timing experiments. These substantially expand procedural documentation. Earlier explicit Imagenette resolution and learning-rate details are omitted; the A100 hardware disclosure already existed.

R1.justification: V2 broadens the cited context to causal interpretation and spurious correlations, diffusion-assisted adversarial training, ImageNet training protocols, and attribution/segmentation methods. These additions go beyond citation-format changes. The core positioning relative to UIAT and MART remains, while the Yu et al. robust-overfitting reference disappears with its analysis.

P1.justification: V2 substantially expands and rewrites the introduction and FLOE explanation, introduces numbered sections and detailed subsections throughout, and reorganizes the supplement around algorithm details and new analyses. Author information and affiliations also change.

P2.justification: V2 restructures Table 1, adds four result tables and Algorithm 1, and removes Figures 9 and 10. Retained tables and figures are relocated and reformatted; Figure 7 changes its reference-region labels from true to normal foreground/background. Caption placement and document layout also change throughout.

improvement.justification: The FLOE sign correction, pseudocode, code link, and broader evaluations improve clarity and coverage. However, new Table 5 labels DHAT's 83.95% as PGD-10 accuracy, whereas Table 1 reports 60.49% PGD-10 and 83.95% clean accuracy. V2 also removes the learning curves still referenced in Section 4.2.3. These problems weaken the central overfitting evidence, leaving the net quality benefit uncertain despite the useful additions.
